title: Rigorix Identity Claims v1
description: v1 (2026-09-07) — grounded in rigorix-oss engine/src/identity/domain/claim.rs (code is truth, contract frozen: serde-stable field names, round-trip preserves every field). Root validates the FULL attributed claim (IdentityClaim) — the output of claim verification on local surfaces (run author, approval service, MCP auth, enterprise JWKS verification). $defs.identityRef is the REDACTED form carried in audit envelopes (never token_ref/auth_method/raw token). IdentitySource serializes snake_case (idp_token | local_principal | unverified) — degradation is a first-class state, never a silent fallback. All Option fields are always serialized (no skip_serializing_if on IdentityClaim): absent values are null, never omitted keys. Raw IdP/JWT claim sets are the INPUT to verification and are not schema-bound here (extension slot: enterprise delta map).

identityClaim.description: Full attributed, time-bound claim — evidence of who was PRESENTED as authorizing, not proof of who the person is.

subject.description: The human's unique identifier at the IdP (e.g. "user@org" or `sub`).

issuer.description: Who vouches for the subject (IdP issuer URL, or "local").

source.description: How identity was established. Unverified = explicit degradation (IdP unreachable / no credential), never a silent fallback.

auth_method.description: Auth method from the token, e.g. device_code, client_credentials.

expires_at.description: When the claim expires. null = no expiry.

token_ref.description: Reference to the raw token for off-band verification. NEVER the raw token value itself (SpanPrivacy) — a store key/id reference.

identityRef.description: REDACTED claim summary (IdentityRef::from_claim) — deliberately copies only summary fields; token_ref, auth_method and the raw token are never carried. This is the shape inside the audit envelope identity block (see envelope.json $defs.identityRef).

authority.description: Always present when serialized by the engine (no serde skip); null when absent.
